brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Two levels of base: half-n bases at level 0 (0,0,0),(1,0,0) and level 1 (0,0,1),(1,0,1), stacked and snapped together (snap pieces at both levels).
Four drawers on the cut faces of the half bases: drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:0#1,0#cut at level 0, drawer:1#0,0#cut and drawer:1#1,0#cut at level 1 (all on slot s).
The build is a freestanding 2x2-cell tower of 4 bases; the configurator has no workbench-mounting part, so how it is fixed to a bench is not modelled. Open cap faces remain (info only, optional).

finish.summary: Built a two-storey tower of four half-north hex bases (two per storey, snapped together) with four drawers on the cut faces, two per storey. check_build reports no rule errors and meshClash is clear. The workbench attachment is not something the configurator models, so that part of the brief is only partly addressed.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
